name: Bleach bypass

influenced_by: a film-lab technique skipping (or partially skipping) the bleach step in processing, which normally removes silver from the negative

eras: technique dates to at least the 1950s-60s; notably used by cinematographer Kazuo Miyagawa for Her Brother (1960)
garments: not a fashion look — a film-processing technique

media.title: Kazuo Miyagawa, Her Brother (1960)
media.note: an early, widely cited use of the technique

media.title: Saving Private Ryan (1998)
media.note: a well-known later use for its desaturated, high-contrast war scenes

reacts_against: nothing — it's a chemical processing choice that leaves some silver in the color negative, producing higher contrast, desaturated color and deeper blacks, used deliberately for a harsher, grittier look.

findings: dark — about 48% of the measured color across 6 Commons photos is below mid-lightness
mostly muted — about 97% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
